proof_audit.judgment: Full-column rank is both necessary and sufficient on unrestricted R^k; the displayed null line covers every competing solution. The Gram positivity argument requires rank(Z′X)=k, while Z full column rank makes its projection defined. P_Z symmetry/idempotence gives two-stage coefficients, not ordinary second-stage residual inference. Basis invariance and inverse-transpose GMM weight changes are dimensionally correct.

The exact error identity precedes consistency and root-n inference. E||zx′|| finite supplies B_n convergence; rank and positive limiting weight supply an invertible neighborhood. The centered iid score has finite second moment. Same-sample weight estimation needs convergence to a fixed matrix, not independent estimation. With G=-B the negative derivative-form multiplier becomes the positive K_W; the fitted-moment projection has the corresponding I-BK sign.

A consistent preliminary coefficient plus E||zx′||² finite makes the average squared score error vanish. Cauchy-Schwarz controls the two cross terms, and E||zu||² finite supplies the remaining LLN. This proof does not silently assume fourth moments of all coordinates. The preliminary estimate must itself meet a consistency theorem; for 2SLS its weight convergence is a separate condition of that application. Recomputing the meat at the second-step estimate changes the finite algorithm.

K_W B=K_* B=I implies DB=0. The efficient cross covariance vanishes, leaving D Omega D′. This proves a PSD difference within the same correct-moment, strong-rank class; it need not be positive definite. A separate two-coefficient example checks the matrix identity rather than only scalar variances.

Positive-definite Omega allows whitening. The derivative span has rank k, so its orthogonal complement has rank m-k. A standard Gaussian projected onto that complement gives the chi-square limit; feasible inverse covariance replacement is o_P(1) because normalized fitted moments are O_P(1). Exact identification gives zero J. Aligned invalidity can fit a shifted target, and weak rank is outside the proof.

Compactness, continuity, measurable global selection and uniform criterion convergence establish consistency under a unique zero before any local rate claim. Interiority and a differentiability ball justify the integrated Jacobian identity. Uniform derivative convergence and full rank make the nonsymmetric finite matrix invertible near its positive-definite limit. This obtains root-n without assuming it. An approximate score residual needs o_P(n^-1/2) plus separate consistency. A square-integrable local envelope justifies the feasible nonlinear score covariance.

The positive square-root domain has a unique zero and correct clipping, derivative and variance. The symmetric domain has two regular roots. The cubic model is globally identified but has derivative zero; inactive clipping with probability tending to one yields n^(1/6) times the estimate converging to the real cube root of a standard normal. No optimizer success restores the missing rank.

Fixed deterministic z normalized by z′z=n and a positive-definite iid disturbance covariance make standardized scores exactly jointly Gaussian at each n. The exact ratio gives a shrinking error for fixed nonzero pi and a nondegenerate nonshrinking law for c/sqrt(n). Correlation between u and v is permitted. An exact zero denominator is probability zero; nearby values retain positive probability.

Under each true candidate, fixed full-rank Z projects the spherical Gaussian structural error; endogenous X is not conditioned on. Known positive variance and no nuisance coefficient give exact chi-square_m and coverage by test inversion. The Gram constraints A>=0, B²<=AC and A=0=>B=0 make every set interval, singleton, empty or all-real. The stated statistic cannot produce disjoint rays. Arbitrary estimated variance or dependent errors cannot inherit this calibration.

Consistency/no interference, independent nondegenerate assignment, exclusion, integrability, individual monotonicity and positive complier mass are explicit. The signed compliance identity yields the Wald ratio for compliers; the covariance form requires its included intercept. Independent assignment probability is stated before ATT calculations. Changing a never-treated counterfactual leaves the whole observed joint law fixed while ATE changes, which is a constructive nonidentification proof.
